Phosphofructokinase (PFK) catalyzes the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, which is the committed step of glycolysis and subject to allosteric regulation by ATP, citrate, and AMP.  
Hexokinase catalyzes the first step but is not generally considered the primary rate-limiting enzyme; phosphorylase is involved in glycogenolysis, not glycolysis; pyruvate dehydrogenase connects glycolysis to the citric acid cycle but is not part of glycolysis itself.  
Thus, PFK is the main rate-limiting enzyme in glycolysis according to standard biochemistry references.
